meta.source: Hand-authored. NOT generated from the workbook.
meta.why: The compendium records what an exercise trains, never how hard it is to do well. Quick workout needs that third axis to keep a beginner away from snatches without hiding them from everyone. Kept out of the generated files for the same reason as hypertrophy.json: tools/extract-workbook.ps1 rewrites those wholesale.
meta.model: A rule per profile, plus a list of the exercises the rule gets wrong. The rule alone cannot tell a Bodyweight Squat from a Pistol Squat -- both are Compound / Bodyweight / Squat / Quads -- so the overrides carry the real judgement and the rule only has to be right about the bulk.
meta.meaning: Tiers are about how much skill and coaching a movement needs before it is worth loading, NOT how hard the set feels. A Leg Press to failure is agony and still basic. Familiarity counts: the barbell squat, bench, deadlift, press, row and pull-up are basic despite being technical, because they are the lifts every beginner programme is built from and every gym has someone who can spot a bad one.
meta.cumulative: basic is a subset of medium is a subset of advanced. Choosing advanced excludes nothing.

rules.comment: Applied when an exercise is in no override list. Also how the user's own exercises are tiered, since nobody is going to hand-rate those.

overrides.comment: Keyed on the English name. A renamed exercise silently falls back to its rule tier rather than breaking -- worth knowing if you edit the workbook.

notes.Kettlebell Swing: Demoted from the Olympic-lift rule. It is the one lift in that profile taught in every commercial gym, and it is a hinge, not a pull under a bar.
notes.Push Press: Same demotion, less strongly: it is an overhead press with legs, and the bar never has to be caught.
notes.Good Morning: Advanced despite being a plain barbell hinge. Loaded spinal flexion is the thing it punishes, and it is the least self-correcting lift here.
notes.plyometrics: The rule puts them at medium because landing mechanics matter. Box Jump, Jump Squat, Pogo Hop and Medicine Ball Slam come back down: they are how you teach the rest.
notes.rings: Anything on rings goes up a tier over its fixed-bar equivalent. The instability is the whole point and it is what makes them unforgiving.
